queries.To select representative synthetic sampl: Greedy maximum coverage approximation for selecting representative LLM-generated synthetic text samples from a similarity graph by pruning edges with a binary search similarity threshold to improve classifier training.
queries.To represent synthetic data relationship: Constructing a similarity graph from pre-trained text embeddings of synthetic LLM-generated training data, where nodes are data points and edges are weighted by pairwise cosine similarity, to support adaptive coverage sampling and representative subset selection for classifier training.
queries.To improve sampling efficiency and diver: coverage-based sampling of synthetic text data using similarity graph with maximum nearest neighbors node outdegree constraint and minimum 0.707 cosine similarity threshold for diverse representative classifier training
queries.To create balanced synthetic training da: balanced synthetic training data generation with GPT-3.5 using prior prompt designs to create equal numbers of examples for each classification label in downstream tasks such as sentiment analysis and relation extraction
queries.To evaluate downstream performance, we w: Downstream evaluation of adaptive coverage sampling for synthetic training data on sentiment analysis and relation extraction, using BERT fine-tuning, synthetic SST2 and FewRel datasets, balanced labels, and accuracy, F1, precision, and recall metrics.
queries.To compare sampling strategies, we will: Evaluation of adaptive coverage sampling against random sampling, k-means clustering-based sampling, full synthetic dataset training, and human-labeled data training for selecting representative subsets of LLM-generated synthetic text to train BERT classifiers
queries.To train classifiers, we will fine-tune: Fine-tuning BERT-base classifiers on coverage-sampled synthetic LLM text subsets using consistent hyperparameters and repeated random seeds for robust evaluation
queries.To identify optimal coverage levels, we: adaptive coverage sampling for synthetic LLM-generated training data, varying target coverage from 0 to 1 to find optimal coverage that improves classifier performance by excluding noisy or less informative samples
queries.To assess performance, we will assess pe: Evaluation metrics for BERT-based sentiment analysis and relation extraction models trained on synthetic data, reporting accuracy, F1, precision, and recall on human-labeled test sets.
queries.To validate the monotonicity assumption,: MNIST experiments validating the monotonicity assumption that coverage increases as similarity thresholds decrease in binary search for max-coverage sampling of embedded data, demonstrating cross-modal applicability of adaptive coverage sampling for synthetic training data downsampling.
